title: Silabs Debug Channel Protocol: Adding support for Wisun Dissection
description:
- Support for Wisun dissection with detailed dissection for Wisun PHR
- Added additional fields for EFR32 Radio Info and fixed bugs

- code clean up

notes.body:
Hi,

Thanks
Look Good, can you share a pcap ?

[test_mode_switch.pcap](/uploads/86c25352d94966b2522d6c896cdf1a38/test_mode_switch.pcap)

This should cover everything related to this change.
called col_add_str with "Wi-SUN FSK Mode Switch PHR" - could call col_set_str() instead (and avoid string copy)

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/19279/diffs?diff_id=1294190396&start_sha=ca2edbfb862eb716945eb8f4d93e7189de7726d2#10db2c38198fc7f05979a1fe2dd968080037fc32_700_700)
I've never used it, but I expect you could use the function in wsutil/bitswap.h (like you do above)?
The wsutil/bitswap.h only exports a function to bit swap a buffer inplace (`bitswap_buf_inplace()`) . I don't think I can use that here.
filter should start with silabs-dch?

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/19279/diffs?diff_id=1294190396&start_sha=ca2edbfb862eb716945eb8f4d93e7189de7726d2#10db2c38198fc7f05979a1fe2dd968080037fc32_1138_1138)

Looking at your capture, I found it confusing that you dissect your bytes first in your tree, even though they come after the 802.15 payload within the frame...

Do you find it easier to analyze the 802.15 payloads this way (which I guess is the main aim of the dissector) ?
I'm assuming you're talking about the elements that I dissect but don't add yet like protocol, appended_info, etc. These are needed to determine the length of the 15.4 payload and are hence required.
I meant the fields that you do dissect that appear after the 802.15 frame, even though they appear before the 802.15 bytes in the frame.  I guess this if fine if you prefer it this way.
Can you please point me to one of the fields you're referring to. I'm a bit confused here, thanks.

I meant HW End, RSSI, Radio Config, Radio Config Extension, Radio Info, Status, Appended Info Config.

If in most cases, the interesting thing is the 802.14 frame, then I understand why its at the root level and therefore appears further down the tree than these fields.

Not an issue for your dissector, but I was also confused by the way the 802.15 dissector writes its 'data' part using the same same top-level tree the 802.15 dissector tree is added at, rather than inside the 802.15 tree...  It looks like the zbee -nwk dissector would be called in the same way.

Maybe what we (as a project) should consider is creating an alternative to call_data_dissector() that also takes a label string...
I could see that being helpful in some cases.
